{"search_note":"I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence of:
- military spending used to enrich networks,
- explicit patronage of security elites,
- or spending mainly for personal image or intimidation unrelated to security.

So the record is strongest on **real-security-needs spending**, with some **escalation/projection** mixed in, and little to support corruption/patronage claims.","evidence":[{"title":"Department of Defense Releases the President's Fiscal Year 2025 Defense Budget","publisher":"U.S. Department of Defense","date":"2024-03-11","url":"https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/3703410/department-of-defense-releases-the-presidents-fiscal-year-2025-defense-budget/","summary":"The FY2025 defense budget was described as strategy-driven, aimed at defending the nation, countering China as the pacing challenge, and funding readiness, procurement, and R&D. This is still defensive in framing, but it shows controlled escalation and signal projection beyond minimal defense.","question_ids":["2B.8","2B.2","2B.5"]},{"title":"Biden allowed U.S.-supplied weapons to be used for counterfire near Kharkiv, while keeping the ban on offensive strikes inside Russia","publisher":"Associated Press","date":"2024-05-30","url":"https://apnews.com/article/czechia-ukraine-russia-nato-blinken-441c9624d95f8193e99cf08effced44f","summary":"The policy was limited and defensive, but it still shows the administration choosing military response alongside diplomacy rather than strictly minimizing mobilization.","question_ids":["2B.8","2B.2","2B.5"]}]}
